packs.title: Steps and Shores
packs.promise: Explore street forms and shoreline landmarks across three Istanbul outings.

q.s: Collect three details from a former bank building.
st: Look at the street facade from a comfortable stopped position on open public pavement, or use Salt’s building photograph.
Find a rough stone block, a window frame and a carved detail. Keep observations to what your chosen view shows.
Save the three details as words or small sketches. Read Salt’s account of the building’s former bank use and mark that as a sourced fact, separate from your observations.

q.s: Collect a pose, an edge and a material contrast.
st: Choose an open public view of the monument, or use the district authority’s photograph. Move to another position or use the photograph if a ceremony occupies the square.
Notice one sculpted pose, one straight stone edge and one contrast between the dark figures and the pale backing. Keep your description to what is visible.
Save the three observations as notes or sketches. Add a small question about how a pose can suggest movement without claiming what the sculptor intended.

q.s: Create a tiny sequence from an opera house’s facade.
st: Look at the facade from an open public stopped position, or use the municipal gallery. Choose a tall arched window and a relief or carved detail.
Make two small frames from those shapes: an arrival and an imagined scene of your own. Do not copy a performance, poster or another artist’s story.
Add a sentence describing what changes between your frames. Simple shapes or a written two-part sequence are enough.

packs.title: Across the Waterline
packs.promise: Follow small details from the old city toward the moving water.

q.s: Collect a curve, a point, and the space between them.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Sultanahmet Park public paths between Ayasofya and Sultanahmet Camii. Keep the route through the space clear.
From outside worship entrances, choose one dome curve, one minaret point, and one gap of sky. You may observe just one building.
Describe how the three shapes fit together without ranking buildings or counting every tower.
Save your three-shape collection in a note or optional exterior photo.

q.s: Write a first impression from ordinary things close by.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Public paths on the northern side of Sultanahmet Park near Divanyolu Caddesi. Keep the route through the space clear.
Find a ground-level texture, a moving shadow or breeze-stirred shape, and a patch of sky. Stay away from entrances and tram tracks.
Write three brief lines, one per observation.
Keep the three lines as a field note, with an optional public-space photo.

q.s: Let a short change of position redraw the waterfront.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Galata Bridge upper pedestrian pavement at its Eminönü end. Keep the route through the space clear.
Use a marked crossing and an open upper pedestrian approach. Walk or roll only as far as comfortable, then stop clear of fishing lines and through traffic; no full crossing is required.
Compare the near shoreline with the opposite bank. Find one low horizontal feature and one rising feature; notice how the space between them changes with your position.
Save two shore details and one change in a field note or optional view photo.
